answer: An agent economy can make each account post a refundable bond before it may place orders, with the bond locked until its trades settle. A reputation score then grows only from completed, non-reversed exchanges with distinct counterparties, not from creating accounts or trading with oneself. Sybils can spiral across the network, like a dune spreading, but each new identity still ties up capital and must attract real counterparties; wash trades risk forfeiting the bond. The delta is that attack scale is limited by capital and settlement time, not cheap account creation.
